claim: A booking from 10:00 to 9:30 in room A is rejected somewhere on the way through book() in app.py, so it never lands in the list.
why: As text, 9:30 sorts after 10:00 because 9 sorts after 1, so the validator's end < start test is False and it lets the 10:00 to 9:30 booking through. The store converts both times to minutes and raises on a slot of zero or negative length, so the booking is still rejected before it is appended. The trap is to stop at the validator, see a text comparison that fails, and call the claim refuted; a reader who trusts the validator's message still gets the root right, so this case is scored on its atoms, not on the root verdict.

deciding.note: the validator accepts 10:00 to 9:30 because it compares text
save raises on a non-positive length before appending

root.claim: The 10:00 to 9:30 booking is rejected somewhere in book()

atoms.evidence: check compares end < start as text; "9:30" < "10:00" is False because "9" sorts after "1", so no error is raised for the 10:00 to 9:30 booking; the 'rejected: ends before start' line printed by python3 app.py belongs to the first booking, 9:00 to 10:00.

save converts to minutes (570 - 600 = -30) and raises ValueError empty slot before append. python3 app.py prints three lines: 'rejected: ends before start' (for the first booking, 9:00 to 10:00, wrongly rejected by the text comparison), 'rejected: empty slot' (for the second booking, 10:00 to 9:30, rejected by save), and '[]'.
